# Leading luxury real estate agencies on the Mornington Peninsula

For prestige residential properties on Victoria’s Mornington Peninsula, I’d start with a shortlist of established luxury brands and strong local operators, particularly those active in **Portsea, Sorrento, Flinders, Red Hill, Mount Eliza and Mount Martha**\.

The key distinction is between an agency with a strong prestige-property brand and an individual agent or auctioneer who can demonstrate success selling multimillion-dollar homes. The best choice depends on the property’s location, price bracket, likely buyer pool and whether you want a public auction or a more discreet sale.

## 1\. Agencies worth shortlisting

![3247 Point Nepean Road, Sorrento VIC 3943 - For Sale by Sorrento](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/dlFxGmt2Ml7erKbcM2Qmf0JBmTP6ypnUk3_3ICySoYytq3_Oqhg9V7bnKEb6u0ScaiDOHJnttOqUIBZEpCPegD2WFt7PHlycK2kZu_XzZByRfekoja-8H0vrZrpSFXPgfZeq2WQNJW93suhlc5Ge8NE5ahWHzK3QkCEeyC_QeW8jmTsUsRtfReHNOEbJPt5G?purpose=fullsize)

(Luxury-brand specialist)

Offices: Sorrento, Mount Eliza and Flinders. ## 3\. What does “top-performing” actually mean?

A high-profile agency or a well-reviewed auctioneer is not automatically the best choice for a \$5 million–\$15 million property. For an evidence-based comparison, I would request the following from each candidate\:

| Measure | What to ask for |
|--------|--------|
| Prestige sales | Comparable sales above your property's likely price bracket over the past 24 months |
| Auction results | Number offered, sold under the hammer, passed in and sold after auction |
| Price performance | Results against the original advertised guide and reserve |
| Buyer reach | Evidence of qualified local, interstate and international buyers |
| Marketing | Specific campaign plan, photography, editorial exposure and database strategy |
| Fees | Commission, auctioneer fee, advertising budget and any additional costs |


For context, Marshall White's published 2025–26 Prestige Property Report records a highest sale price of \$11.3 million for its Peninsula market and 273 sales, with the data covering November 2024 to October 2025. This is a useful indicator of its market presence, but it does not independently establish the best auction clearance rate or highest-performing individual agent. [www.datocms-assets.com](https://www.datocms-assets.com/108926/1764667707-prestige-property-report-2025-2026_digital.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 4\. My shortlist by property type

Trophy home in Portsea or Sorrento

Start with Peninsula Sotheby's International Realty, RT Edgar and Marshall White.

---

Prestige acreage in Flinders or Red Hill

Compare Kay & Burton, Marshall White and Peninsula Sotheby's International Realty.

---

Premium home in Mount Eliza or Mount Martha

Compare Marshall White, Jellis Craig and an experienced local auctioneer such as Peter Kennett or Brett Trebilcock.

---

Dromana, McCrae or Rosebud

Give Grant McConnell and Belle Property serious consideration alongside other agents with recent comparable sales in the immediate area.

These are starting points for interviews, not a claim that any one firm will necessarily achieve the highest price. For the highest-value properties, I'd also compare an auction strategy with an expressions-of-interest campaign or a discreet off-market approach.

search_results.title: Villa Alcyone: Award-winning Elanora mansion eyes suburb record
search_results.description: Villa Alcyone, a Mediterranean-style mansion situated on a steep 890 sqm block at 6 Bicton Ct in Elanora, has entered the market with expectations to surpass the suburb's sales record by millions. Designed by Jayson Pate and built by Resolve Constructions, the award-winning home reflects a growing trend of luxury builders tackling challenging vertical sites. The property garnered multiple accolades at the 2026 HIA Gold Coast and Northern Rivers Awards and a Master Builders Queensland award. The four-bedroom, four-bathroom home spans 579 sqm and features high-end finishes such as Italian marble, dramatic archways, and a Sukabumi stone pool, all inspired by European influences during the owners' travels. Interior design was led by co-owner Helen Foukkare. Positioned to maximize ocean views and offering access to popular nearby beaches like Currumbin and Palm Beach, the mansion is drawing interest from high-end buyers typically focused on more traditionally prestigious areas. Although quarterly data shows a slight dip in Elanora home prices, the suburb's annual values rose 14.7 percent, reflecting its evolving luxury market appeal. The Foukkares are already planning another unique luxury build in the Gold Coast region.

search_results.title: Surfers Paradise mega-penthouse heads to auction as Simon Beard 'meets market'
search_results.description: Simon Beard, founder of Culture Kings, and his wife Tah-nee are putting their luxurious four-level penthouse in Surfers Paradise up for auction after failing to sell it at the original $30 million asking price in 2024. Despite receiving strong offers at the time, Beard held out in hopes of setting a record, a decision he now regrets. With falling national home prices and rising interest rates, the couple is ready to meet the market and sell the property to the highest bidder. The exclusive penthouse atop the Soul building includes five bedrooms, seven bathrooms, panoramic views, a whisky bar, cigar lounge, eight-car garage, balcony gym, and Australia's highest private rooftop pool. Interior highlights feature opulent finishes such as a marble and brass staircase, custom chandeliers, and a $1 million sneaker display. Originally purchased for a record $15.25 million in 2021, the property is listed by agent Tolemy Stevens and will go to private auction on November 20, 2026. The Beards now live in a waterfront mansion nearby with their four children, which they bought for $11.75 million in 2020.

search_results.title: Wealthy Aussie family bears brunt of brutal housing downturn
search_results.description: Australia's luxury property market is experiencing a significant downturn, highlighted by dramatic declines in high-profile home sales. A four-bedroom home in Flinders, Victoria, originally offered at $10.25 million, eventually sold for $7.8 million after 305 days on the market. Similarly, Rothesay, a six-bedroom mansion in Balmain East, Sydney, recently sold for $12.8 million—down nearly 35% from its $19.76 million price in 2022. The owner, businessman Devesh Mishra, had declared bankruptcy following the collapse of his firms, prompting a mortgagee-in-possession sale. Real estate agents cite high interest rates, low buyer inquiries, and financial instability—including inflation and global conflict—as key drivers of the market slump. Experts from Cotality Research and AMP predict property value declines of up to 15%, surpassing earlier forecasts and marking the steepest post-war price fall in Australia. National home values have dropped 5.2% since March, with capital cities like Sydney and Melbourne seeing even steeper declines. Agents suggest deferring property sales until after upcoming elections, hoping for market stabilization.

Why are rough sleepers dying a stone's throw from luxury waterfront houses in Victoria?
search_results.description: In the Mornington Peninsula, Victoria—an area known for its affluence and luxury homes—homelessness is claiming lives at an alarming rate. Over just six weeks, four rough sleepers have died, part of a larger tally of 11 deaths since December 2024. Despite the region having the second highest number of rough sleepers in the state, it suffers from a significant shortage of support services. Outreach workers Leonie and Pete, from the privately funded Southern Peninsula Community Support, report 111 people currently sleeping rough, struggling with mental illness, addiction, and a lack of affordable housing. The area's median rent has soared to $723 per week, exceeding even Melbourne's. Crisis accommodation is limited to a single facility with only seven units. The homeless — including families and working professionals — face years-long waitlists for public housing. Advocates stress that timely housing and mental health support could prevent many deaths. Launch Housing and local support workers urge the government to fund supportive housing. Although the Victorian government has pledged $2.1 million over four years for outreach, experts argue this is insufficient to address the complex, urgent crisis. Without systemic intervention, preventable deaths among the homeless will likely continue.

search_results.title: Port Melbourne industrial modernist home sells for $1.252m
search_results.description:
A distinctive industrial modernist home in Port Melbourne, designed by architect Robert McIntyre, sold for $1.252 million just 10 days after hitting the market. Located at 29 Little Cruikshank St, the two-bedroom residence features full-height windows, raw concrete floors with underfloor heating, timber beams, and a central entrance fissure. Marketed as a "hidden secret" due to its laneway position by agent Nicholas Hoo of Marshall White, the property drew about 120 groups during the campaign. Strong interest led to a quick auction, where four bidders competed, and a soon-to-be owner-occupier clinched the winning bid.

Meanwhile, in Mont Albert North, a four-bedroom house at 19 Arnott St with strong sentimental value also changed hands. Owned by the same family since 1973 and formerly home to Grafico founder Damian Corney’s grandparents, the house sold for $1.62 million after passing in at auction. Retaining original features like Franco Cozzo furniture and a salumi-making cantina, the home invoked nostalgia in the buyers, a young couple. Corney expressed joy that the home would not be demolished, marking the sale as a heartfelt end of an era.

search_results.title: Fire-ravaged Sydney home sparks hot auction
search_results.description: Despite its fire-damaged condition, a former Homes NSW housing commission property at 19 Robertson Street, Merrylands attracted significant interest at auction. With six registered bidders and competitive bidding, the home sold for $1.061 million—above its $1.050 million reserve. This is notable considering broader trends of low auction activity in Sydney, driven by rising interest rates and market uncertainty. Chief Auctioneer Ben Mitchell noted such demand reflects buyer interest in properties with potential, especially near the $1 million price point. Agent Soon Tee highlighted the property's appeal due to its 682 sqm land size and potential for redevelopment, with the buyer intending to construct a house and granny flat. Overall affordability under $1.5 million remains active. Despite overall lower auction clearance rates in Sydney, which sat at 37% in early October due to economic pressures, other high-profile sales also occurred. A Randwick home sold for $3.86 million, and a five-bedroom Bronte property exceeded its reserve by almost $1 million, selling for $12.12 million. These successful sales suggest selective resilience in the Sydney property market.

## 3\. What does “top-performing” actually mean?

A high-profile agency or a well-reviewed auctioneer is not automatically the best choice for a \$5 million–\$15 million property. For an evidence-based comparison, I would request the following from each candidate\:
